name: pixelate-mcp

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: What is open in PixelAOI: the canvas size, the frames and the one on show, the layer stack (layers and folders, top to bottom, with each layer's index and uid and each folder's id) and the selection, the active tool, the palette size, the Blueprint editor's state, and the command names run_command takes.

tools.name: get_canvas_image
tools.description: The current frame as PixelAOI shows it (every visible layer together), as a PNG.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run one of PixelAOI's commands by name: flip_h, flip_v, rotate_90, trim, undo, redo, save and the rest of get_state's commands list. A filter's name (invert, blur, ...) applies it at once with its remembered settings, as one undo step.

action.description: A command name from get_state's commands.

tools.name: apply_filter
tools.description: Apply a filter to the active layer, as one undo step named after it: invert, desaturate, posterize, brightness_contrast, hsl_adjust, levels, curves, gradient_map, palettize, blur, pixelate, outline, drop_shadow, despeckle, convolve, convolve_5x5, color_reduce, palette_variants (the user's variant on show; it has no settings). Settings the call leaves out keep the user's remembered (or default) values. A selection limits it, as in the editor. With output adjustment, every filter but color_reduce becomes an adjustment layer instead: the art stays as it is and the change can be edited or applied later (see adjustment_layer).

name.description: The filter, e.g. blur or hsl_adjust.

params.description: Settings by the labels PixelAOI shows ({"Radius": 3}, {"Hue": 30, "Saturation": -20}) or in order. Curves (an object only): {"all": [[input, output], ...], "red"/"green"/"blue": ...}, 0-255, at most 16 points a channel; channels left out keep the remembered curve. Gradient Map (an object only): {"stops": [[position, r, g, b], ...]}, 0-255, 1 to 16 stops. Palette Cycling (an object only, adjustment output only): {"runs": [{"colours": [[r, g, b], ...], "every": 1, "reverse": false}]}, at most 8 runs of 64 colours, every 1-16 frames a step. Convolve: "Divide by" 0 = Auto (the sum of the weights), 1 = the Divisor; giving a Divisor selects it. Outline and Drop Shadow take their colour as color: [r, g, b].

output.description: Change the layer (default), put the result on a new layer above it, or add an adjustment layer doing it live (every filter but color_reduce; palette_cycling only this way).

affects.description: output adjustment: only the layer under it (default), or everything under it in its folder.

frames.description: Which frames (default: the frame on show).

tools.name: layers
tools.description: Arrange the layer stack: select, move, group, ungroup, new_folder, set, delete, duplicate or merge. Each change is one undo step and every frame follows. Name a layer by its index (as get_state's stack lists it), {layer: index} or {uid: '…'} (the uid text the stack gives, which survives moves); a folder by {folder: id}. Leaving out items acts on the current selection. Folders hold layers and folders (drawn together, then laid down at the folder's opacity) and may be empty. Locked layers and folders stay put, and nothing moves past a locked layer. Returns the stack (top to bottom) and the selection.

action.description: select: choose items; move: put items at a place; group: items into a new folder where the topmost is; ungroup: a folder away, what it held staying; new_folder: an empty folder (default: above the focus); set: change items; delete; duplicate (each copy right above its original); merge: selected layers into the lowest.

items.description: What to act on (default: the selection).

focus.description: select: the one painted and filtered (default: the last named).

above.description: move / new_folder: right above this item, in its folder.

below.description: move / new_folder: right below this item, in its folder.

into.description: move / new_folder: into this folder (its id), or null for the top level.

position.description: With into: the folder's top (default) or bottom.

name.description: group / new_folder: the new folder's name; set: one item's name.

visible.description: set: shown or hidden (a lighting map: used by lighting or not).

opacity.description: set: 0-255 (a folder's own opacity for a folder).

blend.description: set: a layer's blend mode by name (Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Soft Light, …).

draft.description: set: a layer left out of exports.

clipping.description: set: a layer clipped to the one under it.

expanded.description: set: a folder open or folded in the panel.

tools.name: adjustment_layer
tools.description: Adjustment layers: a layer with no art of its own that changes what is under it, live, and can be changed again or applied any time (the art under it stays as it is). add: a new one right above the layer in focus (its mask: the selection, else everything; one mask for every frame). set: change one's settings, its eye (enabled) or what it affects. remove: delete it. bake: apply it to the pixels of what it changes, in every frame, and remove it (refused while another adjustment under it changes the same layers: bake that one first). Kinds: invert, desaturate, posterize, brightness_contrast, hsl_adjust, levels, curves, gradient_map, palette_variants (a copy of the user's variant on show), palettize (snap to a copy of the active palette), palette_cycling (runs of colours stepping once a frame; give its runs as params), outline and drop_shadow (their colour as params color: [r, g, b]), blur, pixelate, despeckle, convolve, convolve_5x5. A new one takes the focus, and filters refuse an adjustment layer in focus: select an art layer before apply_filter. Its strength is the layer's opacity (layers set). Each call is one undo step. Returns the stack (top to bottom) and the selection.

kind.description: add: what it does (levels, hsl_adjust, palettize, ...).

params.description: add / set: settings as apply_filter takes them ({"Hue": 30}, Curves points, Gradient Map stops, Palette Cycling runs); set merges them into its own.

affects.description: add (default layer) / set: only the layer (or folder) right under it, or everything under it in its folder.

enabled.description: set: its eye, on or off.

item.description: set / remove / bake: which adjustment layer (default: the one in focus).

tools.name: set_canvas_image
tools.description: Paint an image (a pixelated PNG, say) into PixelAOI. When it matches the canvas size it paints onto the open document; when not, it opens as a NEW document (as_new_document overrides that). Give exactly one of image_path or png_base64.

image_path.description: Local path to a PNG/JPG/WEBP to paint.

as_new_document.description: A new document (true) or onto the open canvas (false). Default: by size.

name.description: The new document's name, when one is made.

tools.name: set_pixels
tools.description: Paint a raw RGBA block onto the canvas at (x, y), clipped to the canvas. rgba_base64 is base64 of exactly w*h*4 RGBA bytes (row by row, from the top left).

tools.name: pixelate_image
tools.description: Turn an image into grid-perfect pixel art with PixelAOI's own engine, on this computer (it finds the native grid and palette), then paint it into PixelAOI. No cloud and no key. Give exactly one of image_path, png_base64 or image_url.

image_path.description: Local path to the source image (png/jpg/webp).

image_url.description: A URL to fetch the image from.

auto.description: Find the native grid and palette (default true).

colors.description: A palette size; leave out for auto.

target_width.description: The output width (when auto is off).

target_height.description: The output height (when auto is off).

output_path.description: Also save the pixelated PNG here.

paint.description: Paint the result into PixelAOI (default true).

as_new_document.description: A new document (true) or onto the open canvas (false).

name.description: The new document's name, when one is made.

tools.name: extrude_animate
tools.description: Animate the canvas as a 3D extrusion turntable: the silhouette is extruded and turned across the timeline, one frame per step, built for you. A heart that turns side to side, a coin that spins.

ping_pong.description: Swing back and forth (default true), or one sweep.

tools.name: blueprint_node_kinds
tools.description: Every kind of node a Blueprint graph can take, by category (use these names with blueprint_add_node). This is the catalog, not the nodes in the graph (see blueprint_list). The active graph's, or another kind's with graph.

graph.description: The graph kind to ask about; the active graph's when left out.

tools.name: blueprint_list
tools.description: The active Blueprint graph: its kind, its nodes (id, kind, position, data), its links and each parameter's value wire.

tools.name: blueprint_select_graph
tools.description: Make a Blueprint graph kind active (Particle, Canvas, Ai or Layer) and return its summary. Do this before adding nodes, so they land in the right graph.

graph.description: The graph kind to make active.

tools.name: blueprint_add_node
tools.description: Add a node to the active Blueprint graph; returns its id. kind is a node kind's name, e.g. (Canvas graph) CanvasNoise, CanvasGradient, CanvasShape, CanvasFilter, CanvasColorAdjust, PaletteMap, CanvasOutput; (Particle graph) Emitter, Forces, Lifetime. See blueprint_node_kinds for them all.

kind.description: The node kind, e.g. CanvasNoise or CanvasOutput.

tools.name: blueprint_connect
tools.description: Wire node from's output into node to's input in the active graph (checked against the graph's rules).

tools.name: blueprint_connect_value
tools.description: Wire a value node (ValueConstant, ValueSine, ValueMath, …) to drive a parameter of another node: a value wire. param is a parameter's name (e.g. NoiseScale); leave it out to drive the target's main one.

to.description: The node whose parameter it drives.

param.description: The parameter to drive; the target's main one when left out.

tools.name: blueprint_set_data
tools.description: Set a node's settings that aren't numbers (blend mode, shape kind, source mode, sizes, …). Call blueprint_list, copy that node's data object, change the fields you want, and pass the whole object back. Its shape must match the node's.

data.description: The node's whole data object (from blueprint_list), with your changes.

tools.name: blueprint_set_param
tools.description: Set a node's number parameter: NoiseScale, FilterStrength, GradientAngle, ShapeSize, ThresholdLevel, Hue, OffsetX, OffsetY, Rate, Speed, Lifetime, … The value is kept within the parameter's range.

value.description: Its new value (kept within its range).

tools.name: blueprint_delete_node
tools.description: Delete a node, and the links touching it, from the active graph.

tools.name: blueprint_bake
tools.description: Run the active Blueprint graph and bake what it makes into the document: the canvas, a layer or the timeline, as its output node says.

tools.name: add_frame
tools.description: Add a blank frame right after the one on show and show it, as the timeline's + does (one undo step). Paint it with set_canvas_image or set_pixels, which write the active layer of the frame on show.

tools.name: select_frame
tools.description: Show a frame (from 0), as clicking it in the timeline does; the canvas and the painting tools then work on it.

tools.name: set_frame_duration
tools.description: How long a frame shows when the animation plays, 10 to 10000 milliseconds; the frame on show when index is left out.

index.description: The frame, from 0; the one on show when left out.

tools.name: add_tag
tools.description: Tag a run of frames, from and to included (an animation such as idle or walk), as the timeline does.

to.description: The last frame (from, when left out).

tools.name: save_document
tools.description: Save the open document as a PixelAOI project (.pxl) at an absolute path, without a dialog. It becomes the document's file, as Save As does.

tools.name: close_document
tools.description: Close the open document's tab once it is saved (refused while it has unsaved changes: save_document first). The next tab comes up, or Home after the last.

instructions:
PixelAOI is a pixel-art editor running on this computer; these tools drive it. They reach it over a local link the user turns on in PixelAOI: its status bar says "agent off" until clicked, "agent ready" while it waits, "agent live" once you are connected. If a call can't reach it, ask the user to click that pill.
- Start with get_state: the canvas size, the frames, the layer stack (with each layer's index and uid), the selection, the active tool and the command names run_command takes. Look with get_canvas_image before and after changes.
- Every change is one undo step in the editor, with a name; run_command "undo" takes the last one back.
- Frames count from 0. set_canvas_image and set_pixels paint the active layer of the frame on show; add_frame, select_frame, set_frame_duration and add_tag build animations.
- Blueprints (node graphs): blueprint_select_graph, blueprint_node_kinds, blueprint_add_node, blueprint_connect / blueprint_connect_value, blueprint_set_param / blueprint_set_data, then blueprint_bake.
- PixelAOI refuses changes while one of its dialogs or a filter is open, or while the user is drawing; the error says which. Ask the user to finish, then try again.
